top_signals.title: TTF Gas Hits $92.95 as Gulf Tensions Weigh on Energy Markets
top_signals.summary: Europe’s benchmark natural gas prices held above the 80-euro mark early on Wednesday, staying close to 2022 highs, as low gas volumes in storage sites fuel concerns about winter supplies amid continued disruption and widening conflict in the Middle East. The front-month price at the Dutch Title Transfer Facility (TTF), the benchmark for Europe’s gas trading, rose by 0.3% to $$92.95 (80.545 euros) per megawatt-hour (MWh) as of 9:15 a.m. in Amsterdam on Wednesday. top_signals.title: This Is Not Your Father’s Nuclear Flight Test Vehicle
top_signals.summary:
For decades, the United States’ nuclear weapons enterprise has wrestled with an institutional paradox. On one hand is the imperative to make the complex more “responsive” to global tumult and technical surprise, able to field new weapons quickly in reaction to unanticipated threats. On the other are the unforgiving engineering requirements of thermonuclear warheads, devices whose development is measured in years. No silver bullet solution to this unstoppable-force-meets-immovable-object conundrum will likely present itself. top_signals.summary:

She had marked me, correctly, as someone who spoke her language. By the end of the night, she was pressing the body of her dead child into my chest and telling me, “You did this.” I have spent five years with that sentence.In a way, she was wrong about me. top_signals.summary: Turkish stocks tumbled on Wednesday and triggered a market-wide circuit breaker, as an asset manager’s failure to meet redemption requests fueled concern about broader liquidity stress in the country’s investment fund industry.

top_signals.title: United States on track for record crude oil production in 2026
top_signals.summary: We forecast U.S. crude oil production will average 13.8 million barrels per day (b/d) in 2026, surpassing the previous record of 13.7 million b/d set in 2025, in our latest Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO).

top_signals.title: New England natural gas prices have been trading near record discounts to Henry Hub
top_signals.summary: Low-cost Appalachian and Canadian natural gas supplies coupled with lower-than-usual regional consumption have pushed down natural gas prices at a major New England pricing hub in recent months to trade at a discount to the widely cited U.S. benchmark, Henry Hub.
